results.summary: Brailliance converts an ASCII character into its 8-bit Braille representation, where the first two bits of each output byte are zeroed for redundancy. The design is implemented in Verilog and uses a 5 MHz clock. External hardware such as LEDs or solenoid actuators can be used to display the Braille output. This project serves as an educational tool for ASCII-to-Braille conversion.
The design implements a two-player Pong game that uses two NES controllers for input and outputs a VGA video signal.
Munch displays a munching squares animation on a VGA monitor while generating simple music through an audio PMOD.
This experiment implements a 512-bit shift register using D latches instead of flip-flops, with a single pulse rippling through the register to perform the shift.

This design bundles four educational modules selected by an internal multiplexer: a vending machine state machine, a coin acceptor decoder, a 24-bit ripple carry adder, and a 24-bit carry lookahead adder. The adders are tested by feeding 24-bit operands in 8-bit chunks and reading the 25-bit result in 8-bit chunks. An oscilloscope can be used to measure the difference in execution speed between the two adder types. The coin acceptor decoder is designed for the HX-916 model.
The project generates a pseudo-random soundtrack via PWM and displays a waveform on a VGA monitor.

This design is a clock divider with lag correction that interfaces with PDM microphones and an I2S receiver. It takes bit clock and LR clock inputs, along with PDM data from up to eight microphones, and outputs PCM audio for each microphone plus a beamformed PCM output. The documentation is too vague to describe its exact operation.
Comm_IC combines UART, SPI, and I2C communication protocols into a single design that is selected via input data bits.
Crispy VGA takes a VGA signal as input and adds programmable random noise to the video and audio signals before passing them to the output.
This circuit computes the inverse S-box of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), taking an 8-bit input and producing an 8-bit output.
